messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0119", "row_sha256": "2bb6e05358ebdb374ebd0070b9e3fdacbd07267c54830e22e6d11c1561756bc4", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "i'm trying to get a useful brief together for the person who will update the Harbor Street Reading Circle website. this is for the autumn 2025 cycle, not a redesign of the whole site. please ask them to draft the landing page copy and a simple page outline, with enough detail that our volunteer who updates the site can place each part. we need something that works for someone who has never come to the club as well as people who already know us. the main thing is making the dates, sign-up and expectations easy to find. don't write the finished page in this brief, just give the writer a clear assignment.

we meet at Mariner Library, in the Birch Room on the second floor. the side entrance has an elevator, so mention that route plainly, not as a big accessibility claim. meetings are Thursdays from 7:00 to 8:15 p.m. for six weeks, beginning September 4 and ending October 9, 2025. registration opens August 12 and closes August 29, unless all 24 places fill first. if those places are gone, the page should say registration is full and offer a waitlist; it mustn't imply that a person on the list has a seat. the club is free. put the schedule and the capacity where readers won't have to search through a long welcome paragraph.

the cycle's book is A House Made of Weather by N. Vale. readers should know that the club is discussing that one book across the six meetings, not asking them to bring a different book each week. we have eight library copies available to borrow, but don't say that everyone is guaranteed one or that the club will provide all copies. other readers can find or borrow their own copy. don't invent a chapter-by-chapter schedule because we haven't set one. we want newcomers to know they can still join the conversation even if they are a little behind, though they should avoid spoilers past the point the group has reached.

for the actual writing, keep it neighborly and direct, not salesy, grand or too clever. explain what happens at a normal meeting: a guided discussion of the book, time to hear different interpretations, and a few minutes at the end for next week's reading. that's what the meetings include, so don't promise author appearances, refreshments, prizes or special guests. please use everyday words and short blocks of copy, and don't make the club sound like a class where anyone is tested. regular members can contribute, but make it clear that someone can come along and listen before speaking if that's more comfortable.

there's a sentence from member Lena Ortiz that we'd like to use as a small pull quote somewhere on the page: “I finished it on the bus and missed my stop.” keep those exact words and her name together. don't turn it into a general claim about what every member feels. also include a short explanation of the discussion approach: people can disagree about the book, listen to each other, and keep comments about the text rather than judging another reader. we want that to feel welcoming without writing a long list of rules or making it sound like a warning.

for joining, include a numbered section because the steps are easy to mix up. first, complete the form with a name and email address; second, choose whether to opt in to the optional monthly newsletter; third, watch for the confirmation email. the newsletter choice shouldn't be presented as a condition of registration. if the form can't accept any more registrations, direct people to the waitlist instead. don't invent a deadline for the waitlist or say when a place might open. the registration period and the six-week meeting dates should be distinct, so no one mistakes the closing date for the first meeting.

under the page outline, include the order you'd recommend for the information: a brief welcome and cycle description, then the book and meeting details, the numbered joining steps, and finally the location and contact information. the contact is readingcircle@harborstreet.org. label a link to the form “Register for the autumn cycle,” and label a link to the waitlist “Join the waitlist” only when registration is full. don't create extra links, a phone number, a map URL or social media details; we haven't supplied those. the page outline should be practical rather than a visual redesign proposal, and no code is needed.

please also note what the volunteer needs to be able to update: whether registration is open or full, the number of places, and the waitlist link when needed. we don't have an automated live count confirmed, so don't describe the number of remaining seats as updating in real time. the page should state the total capacity of 24 and the open and close dates, but avoid inventing a current availability status. if the writer needs to mention how to ask a question, use the email address above and nothing else.

for readability, make the outline account for mobile readers by keeping the key date, time and registration details near the top and making link labels descriptive. include the elevator route in the location information. don't claim the room has equipment, sign language interpretation or other accommodations we haven't confirmed. the assignment should ask for plain, accessible language and meaningful headings, without asking the writer to build or audit the website. after the draft is ready, send the preview link to Soraya, not Orson. that's just who should receive it; don't add either person as a club contact on the page. finish the brief with what the writer should hand over: landing page copy plus the simple ordered outline, not a new club policy or a full site plan.", "output": "Draft the landing page copy and a practical, ordered page outline for the Harbor Street Reading Circle website’s autumn 2025 cycle. This is an update to one landing page, not a redesign of the whole site. Write for both first-time visitors and returning members. Make the dates, registration process, and meeting expectations easy to find. Do not write code or create a full site plan or new club policies.

Use a neighborly, direct tone. Keep the language plain, the paragraphs short, and the headings meaningful. Avoid sales language, grand claims, and a classroom-like tone. Explain that meetings include a guided discussion of the book, time to hear different interpretations, and a few minutes to review the following week’s reading. Let readers know they can listen before speaking and can join even if they are a little behind; ask them to avoid spoilers beyond the point the group has reached. Describe disagreement as welcome when people listen to each other and discuss the text rather than judge other readers. Do not promise author appearances, refreshments, prizes, or special guests.

Keep the key dates, time, and registration information near the top, especially for mobile readers. State that the club is free and that the six Thursday meetings run from 7:00 to 8:15 p.m., September 4 through October 9, 2025. Registration opens August 12 and closes August 29, unless all 24 places fill first. Distinguish the registration dates from the meeting dates. State the total capacity, but do not invent a current availability status or describe remaining places as a live count. If registration is full, say so and offer the waitlist without implying that joining it guarantees a seat or specifying when one might open.

Identify the cycle’s book as *A House Made of Weather* by N. Vale. Explain that the group discusses this one book over six meetings, rather than asking members to bring a different book each week. Eight library copies are available to borrow, but do not guarantee a copy to anyone or imply the club provides all copies; other readers can find or borrow their own. Do not invent a chapter-by-chapter schedule.

Include this pull quote with Lena Ortiz’s name, preserving the wording exactly: “I finished it on the bus and missed my stop.” Present it as her comment, not as a claim about every member.

Include a numbered joining section:
1. Complete the form with a name and email address.
2. Choose whether to opt in to the optional monthly newsletter. Newsletter signup is not a condition of registration.
3. Watch for the confirmation email.

When registration is open, label the form link “Register for the autumn cycle.” When registration is full, direct readers to the waitlist and label its link “Join the waitlist.” Do not invent a waitlist deadline or a time when a place may open.

For location and contact details, state that meetings take place in the Birch Room on the second floor of Mariner Library and that the side entrance has an elevator. Use readingcircle@harborstreet.org for questions. Do not add a phone number, map URL, social media details, or claims about equipment, interpretation, or other unconfirmed accommodations.

Order the page outline as follows: a brief welcome and cycle description; the book and meeting details; the numbered joining steps; and location and contact information. Keep the outline practical, not a visual redesign proposal. Note that the volunteer should be able to update whether registration is open or full, the total number of places, and the waitlist link when needed. Do not imply that the site has an automated live count.

After the draft is ready, send the preview link to Soraya, not Orson. Do not list either person as a club contact on the page. Hand over the landing page copy and the simple ordered outline."}]
